final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No genuinely new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor instead reinterpreted the existing record into a narrower, caveated position. That narrowing is analytically sound as a description of what the current evidence could support, but it is not enough to make the locked certification decision compliant on this record. Under the policy, certification without material caveats requires either evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The available summary still shows an unresolved named-use-case weakness and only a draft mitigation. A caveated posture could potentially support compliant_with_caveats only if there were admissible evidence that the caveat or disclosure was actually adopted in the final launch record or otherwise approved. That evidence is absent here. The remaining issue is therefore not cured by explanation alone, and the certification decision remains inadequately supported and noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: The field-service dispatch weakness in technician safety-note routing remains unresolved for a named launch use case.
The cited mitigation artifact is still a draft and lacks the required owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion.
There is no new admissible evidence that the limitation is actually disclosed in the final model card or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness, but not certification compliance under the stated policy when a material weakness remains.
The Actor's response narrows and caveats the claim, but it reframes the same evidence rather than satisfying the missing policy predicate.
